inputs.share_count_basis: 478.0M: 478.012M shares issued and outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet; cover page 478.045M at 2026-10-12). Dilutive securities are negligible - Q3 weighted diluted 478.978M vs basic 478.970M, the gap to period-end being the July-August buyback, not dilution. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it. ROL is a funded repurchaser: $140.0M of open-market buybacks in 9M-2026 (3.49M shares at $40.10, $120M of it in Q3) on top of ~$23M withholding; FY2025 $216.9M total.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $39.707M + $18.6M cash tax withheld on net-share settlement. ROL reports withholding inside 'Cash paid for common stock purchased'; the Q3-2026 10-Q states there were no open-market repurchases in the first nine months of 2025, so the whole 9M-2025 line ($18.573M) is withholding (the prior version used the H1 figure, ~$15M). No combined SBC-plus-withholding figure is published, so the two lines are summed. 2026 run-rate is higher: TTM SBC $41.6M (Q3-2026 leverage reconciliation) plus 9M-2026 withholding $22.9M ($162.9M paid less $140.0M open market) = ~1.6% of FY2026E revenue, which anchors sbc_pct_path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.80 (defensive, recurring-service revenue) -> cost of equity 8.2%. Debt ~$727M (2035 senior notes $500M + commercial paper $240M at 4.17%) vs ~$18B market cap (~4% of capital), 2026 interest guided ~$40M -> after-tax ~4%. WACC ~8.0%. UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 version. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a per-scenario rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases (fleet vehicles, branches; FY2025 operating lease payments $159.1M) are expensed inside operating income and therefore inside EBITDA. Lease cost is in the flows; operating lease liabilities are therefore NOT in net debt. One treatment, applied once. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already inside the EBITDA margin.
inputs.acquisition_treatment: ROL is a serial acquirer ($310M FY2025, $157M FY2024, $367M FY2023; $163M in 9M-2026). Acquisitions are treated as NPV-neutral and excluded from BOTH sides: growth from FY2027 onward is ORGANIC plus only the rollover of deals already paid for, and no acquisition spend is charged. FY2026 (year 1) growth includes the 2-3% inorganic contribution guided, because those deals (Romex $95.7M in Apr-2026, Saela rollover, other 9M-2026 tuck-ins) were paid for before the 2026-09-30 balance sheet that sets net debt; FY2027 carries ~0.5pp of Romex/2026 rollover. Any value creation from M&A above WACC is upside not in the base case; overpaying is an uncharged risk. UNCHANGED treatment.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company - recurring pest/termite services, asset-light, no bank/REIT/holdco features). Same model as the 2026-10-02 version; this is an UPDATE for the Q3-2026 10-Q, see `reconciliation`. ANCHORS REFRESHED: price (regular close, not after-hours); net debt 598.1 = commercial paper 239.6 + senior notes 487.6 - cash 129.1 at 2026-09-30; shares 478.0M. CORRECTION: the prior version's total debt (487.1) was the long-term notes only and omitted $215.9M of commercial paper shown as short-term debt at 2026-06-30 (the Metrics total_debt column carries long-term debt only) - worth -$0.44/share, shown separately in the bridge. Withholding estimate for FY2025 corrected $15M -> $18.6M, so owner FCF FY2025 = 650.0 - 39.7 - 18.6 - 0 interest income (net debt, no strip) = 591.7 (15.7% of revenue). DRIVERS RE-JUDGED and why: (1) FY2026 guidance year - outlook cut a second time in Q3 to 4-6% organic (from >=6%; originally 7-8%) with 2-3% from deals unchanged and adjusted incremental EBITDA margin 'slightly positive to 10%' (from >=10%); 9M revenue +8.0% (5.5% organic), Q3 organic 4.4%, so FY2026 growth 8.5% -> 7.5% and pre-SBC EBITDA margin 22.8% -> 22.5% (9M-2026: operating income 569.7 + D&A 99.4 + SBC 31.8 = 700.9, 22.8% vs 24.2% in 9M-2025; Q4 is the seasonally weakest quarter). (2) Later-year growth - the prior version said persistent residential weakness would make 6-6.5% organic too high; Q3 residential organic fell to 2.3% (3.6% in Q2), termite/ancillary to 5.3% (8.9%), commercial to 6.6% (7.2%), and management now describes a changed customer-acquisition landscape (AI/LLM discovery). Base organic lowered to ~4.5-5.5%. (3) Later-year margin - with less growth there is less route-density leverage, and insurance/claims cost (+160bp of revenue in Q3) joined fleet and medical as a drag; base mature margin 24.5% -> 24.0%, bear floor 22.0% -> 21.5%, bull still 26% but a year later. (4) SBC incl. withholding path re-anchored 1.45% -> 1.6% on 2026 actuals. (5) Weights 20/50/30 -> 25/50/25. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: WACC 8.0%, terminal growth 3.0/3.5/2.5, 20x terminal cap, D&A path (TTM 3.3%; would move on a large deal changing intangible amortisation), capex 0.8% (9M-2026 0.65%; left conservative), cash tax 25% (9M ETR 24.1% on purchased transferable credits, guided 'under 25%'; the $63M Q3 refund is timing and is not carried forward), wc_capture 0 (unearned revenue +$4M in 9M), lease and acquisition treatment, 10-year horizon, 15% hurdle. Year-1 component check: owner FCF ~$635M on ~$4.04B revenue = 15.7%, equal to the FY2025 actual 15.7% - nothing unrepeatable carried forward. Timing convention: FY0 is FY2025 and FY2026 is discounted one full year although nine months of it are already in the 2026-09-30 net debt; the over-discounting of every later flow by ~0.9 year more than offsets that, so the convention is mildly conservative and is kept for comparability with the prior version.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic revenue growth: FY2026 guidance 4-6% organic (9M actual 5.5%, Q3 4.4%); the ex-M&A rate is used because the model charges no acquisition spend. Below the 7-8% medium-term target, which two consecutive guidance cuts have not supported
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.7% 3yr / 7.3% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (11.7%) and EPS (13.3-15.1%). Book value is not the growth signal here: ROL pays out ~60% of earnings as dividends and spent $315M (FY2023 secondary-offering repurchase) and $217M (FY2025) on buybacks, so equity barely compounds. Revenue CAGR is itself inflated by ~3pp/yr of acquired revenue, so the selected rate is organic-only.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding: FY2020 383.4 (COVID tax/payroll deferrals inflate it), FY2022 407.0, FY2025 591.7. Owner-FCF CAGR (13.3% 3yr) runs below reported (14.3%): SBC plus withholding rose from ~1.05% to ~1.55% of revenue over FY2022-25 (and ~1.6% in 2026), so a small and growing share of reported growth is paid in stock.

base.narrative: Guidance-anchored: FY2026 ~7.5% total growth (about 5% organic, the middle of the cut 4-6% range, plus 2-3% from deals already paid for). Organic growth then recovers only partway from the Q3 exit rate of 4.4% to ~5-5.5% as Orkin reallocates marketing away from the traditional digital playbook, and fades to 3.5% - well short of the 7-8% medium-term target. Commercial and termite/ancillary keep outgrowing residential. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from 22.5% to 24.0% by Y7 (FY2025: 23.7%) as insurance/claims and fleet costs normalise, with the 30-35% incremental-margin target not delivered.

bull.narrative: Management's medium-term frame is delivered, a year later than previously assumed: the marketing reallocation (including visibility in AI/LLM-driven discovery) restores residential customer acquisition, organic growth returns to 7-7.5% by FY2028-29 with commercial and termite/ancillary leading, and 30-35% incremental margins lift pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 26% as claims, medical and fleet inflation normalise and integration synergies land.

bear.narrative: The residential customer-acquisition problem is structural: search and AI answer engines intermediate the top of the funnel, ad costs rise, PE-backed roll-ups and Rentokil compete on price for local customers, and the Q3 slowdown in termite/ancillary (5.3% from 8.9%) proves to be cross-sell drying up with new-customer flow. Organic growth settles at ~3% (price only). Insurance/claims, medical, fleet and technician-wage inflation are not passed through, so the margin drifts to 21.5% and stays there. No balance-sheet stress: leverage is 1.0x on the company's lease-adjusted measure.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised again, 20% -> 25%: Q3-26 brought a second guidance cut, residential organic growth of 2.3%, and the first deceleration in termite/ancillary, and management now describes the customer-acquisition landscape as changed rather than a quarter's miss - the bear mechanism is the one being observed. Base 50% as the guidance-anchored partial recovery. Bull cut 30% -> 25%: it needs the marketing reallocation to work AND the incremental-margin target to be delivered, neither yet evidenced, but it remains management's stated frame and the retention base is intact. No solvency or refinancing risk justifies a heavier bear. The paths and the weights both moved; the paths carry what Q3 showed, the weights carry the lower odds of the unchanged bull destination.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Rollins is a high-quality, low-capital-intensity recurring-service compounder whose organic growth has decelerated for three straight quarters on a residential customer-acquisition problem. The valuation strips the acquisition engine out (organic growth plus paid-for rollover only, no deal spend) so that the price is tested against what the existing route base earns, charges SBC plus equity-award withholding as a real cost, and caps the terminal value at 20x owner FCF. On that basis the shares, which have recovered from their October low while guidance was cut again, trade above the probability-weighted house value and above the base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Residential organic growth: 2.3% in Q3-26 and falling; if the marketing reallocation does not restore customer acquisition, base-case ~5% organic is too high
Margin: insurance/claims, fleet and medical costs took 140bp off 9M-26 operating margin; base assumes recovery to 24.0% pre-SBC EBITDA, about the FY2025 level
Terminal value is the majority of EV and the 20x cap binds in the base and bull cases; a lower market multiple for slower-growth pest control would cut value directly
M&A treated as NPV-neutral: overpaying in a bid-up market for tuck-ins would destroy value the model does not charge; disciplined buying above WACC is unmodelled upside
Commercial paper ($240M, ~30-day paper) now funds buybacks and deals; small against ~$900M EBITDA but it is rate-sensitive and was missed in the prior version
Equity-award withholding is inferred from the share-purchase line less disclosed open-market repurchases
